candidates.finding: Assessment S2=C observes first-party conflicting task/capsule scope admission and explicitly calls out possible concurrent admission races. Predict two overlapping TASK_CREATE RPC calls could both pass an unreserved scope check; falsify with serialized/atomic admission or a design that forbids the concurrent path.

Assessment S2=C observes a shared interactive confirmation queue across concurrent child agents. Predict an aborted or rejected predecessor could stall the sibling prompt queue; falsify if first-party serializer always recovers and progresses or abort cancels the whole parent by contract.

Assessment S2=C observes per-task mutable agent clones that share a common run-wide budget. Predict simultaneous clones might both pass a stale remaining-budget admission and overspend the shared cap; falsify if charge/reservation is already atomic or budget intentionally advisory.

Assessment S2=C observes thread-based skill-library write serialization and atomic JSON index replacement. Predict two independently supported processes sharing the library may both commit from stale snapshots and lose one skill; falsify if process sharing unsupported or cross-process synchronization already exists.

Assessment S2=C observes path-keyed exclusive write/rename coordination among concurrent tool actors. Predict legal alias-equivalent output paths may take separate locks yet resolve to the same destination; falsify if canonical identity is used or aliases rejected by the supported first-party tool.
